reviewed_by: Claude review of DSML tool-call recovery
reason: Some OpenRouter routes serialize a DeepSeek model's DSML tool calls into the Chat Completions content field instead of tool_calls. Core recognised the frame and quarantined it, which discarded the work the model had asked for and sent the turn into final-answer recovery. This adds a parser (src/nebula/v3/dsml.py) that reads a complete frame back into ordinary tool calls, and a ModelResponse validator that applies it wherever a response is built, so every adapter, streaming or not, reports the calls in tool_calls and the frame leaves the text. Recovered calls take the same broker, policy and approval path as any other call; the parser executes nothing. Parsing is all-or-nothing per frame: a fragment, prose inside a call, a repeated or unnamed argument, an identity no tool can have, or an oversized frame is left in the text exactly as it arrived, and the existing quarantine, now sharing the parser's grammar, still refuses it. test_dsml.py covers the grammar (both pipes, both escape spellings, several invokes and frames, prose around a frame, JSON-typed and literal values, every unreadable shape, the size bound) and the ModelResponse hook (idempotent on re-validation, merging with route-reported calls, leaving unreadable text for quarantine). test_chat_tool_loop.py proves a frame at a routing step runs its tool through the broker, that a readable frame at final synthesis is recovered as a late tool call, and that an unreadable one is still quarantined. test_chat.py and test_providers.py are selected because they construct ModelResponse on every path the validator now runs on.
exclusions: Full Python, frontend and Playwright suites are excluded. No frontend or Playwright test is selected because no UI changed: a recovered call reaches the transcript as the ordinary tool call it already renders. No native tests are selected because no Rust changed. No real-Core entry is selected: reproducing the route requires a live OpenRouter DeepSeek endpoint that CI does not have, and the provider contract the parser relies on is exercised directly on ModelResponse.
